Redwood and VelocityBridge exploring partner integration for Redwood to onboard VelocityBridge as a channel/onramp partner. Primary asks from VelocityBridge: clear private deployment options (VPC, onprem?), predictable GPU capacity and routing, how Redwood handles multi-tenant routing/costing for resellers, security artefacts (SOC2, KMS, audit logs), and a pilot to validate perf for 1k concurrent chat sessions at 2k token lengths. --- Transcript body (selected excerpts, imperfect ASR, filler/crosstalk included) ---
[00:00] Nora (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll give a 20 minute intro then deep dive on the technical bits. quick intros?
[00:10] Samir (VelocityBridge): yeah hi i'm Samir, i run cloud partnerships at VelocityBridge, we connect enterprise SaaS to GPU capacity and were looking at Redwood as a potential inference supplier and partner.
[00:20] Lena: lena here, CTO. main goal is to understand integration patterns and compliance story.
[00:27] Mark: mark, lead systems, i'll be the primary tech contact.
[00:30] Diego (Redwood SE): Diego, solutions eng. happy to walk through network and perf questions.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): priya here, i'll own pilot ops and the benchmark wiring.

[01:00] Samir: to start, are you thinking about a reseller model or pure marketplace slot? we want both—some customers will want VB managed and some want self-serve.
[01:10] Nora: great q. Redwood supports hosted API for fastest time-to-value, Dedicated pools for reserved capacity, and Private (VPC / on‑prem) where customers or partners can run a private control plane. For partner mode there are two common patterns: 1) VelocityBridge as a channel — you re-sell calls through Redwood hosted endpoints and get usage reporting; 2) Onramp — routing layer that forwards eligible requests from VB to Redwood Dedicated capacity, with billing reconciliation.
[01:30] Samir: ok that sounds flexible. on the onramp pattern how do you do routing? we need routing per-tenant because our marketplace will tag requests.
[01:40] Diego: we have policy-based smart routing — you can route by latency SLA, cost tier, or region. policies can match on tenant tags or headers. if a tenant has a pinned model we honor that; otherwise automatic fallback to a compatible model variant.
[01:55] Mark: what's the KV cache story? we do a lot of multi-turn chat and want minimal repeated compute.
[02:05] Diego: we do prefix and KV caching — though the cache semantics depend on the deployment. in hosted mode it's shared but partitioned; in dedicated/private you get tenant-isolated KV cache. note: sometimes logs say K-V cash in transcripts :)
[02:15] Lena: heard you mention quant profiles and batching — we have latency-sensitive agents so batching aggressiveness is a concern.
[02:25] Priya: right — Redwood Optimize suggests batching config per workload. you can set latency SLOs and the runtime will trade-off batch size vs per-request latency. there's also per-route overrides.

[03:10] Samir: security—SOC2? KMS? SSO? audit logs? we have regulated customers.
[03:20] Nora: yes SOC2 Type II available — we'll share the security pack. for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM; VPC peering and private link patterns are supported. SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC to restrict who can deploy models or view tokens. Audit logs available with configurable retention.
[03:40] Ivy (VelocityBridge): any limitations on HSM integrations? we use HashiCorp Vault in our stack.
[03:48] Diego: we integrate with common KMS via API—HashiVault is a frequent integration; for on‑prem HSM we can align via our support tier. we'll flag some ops steps in the security pack.

[05:00] Mark: perf targets — we're thinking 1k concurrent chat sessions, average 2k tokens, 4 requests per session, tail latency 99th < 600ms if possible, cost target is... TBD but we want guidance.
[05:15] Priya: piloting a subset makes sense. we can run a perf harness against a dedicated pool. question: do you have preferred GPU families?
[05:22] Mark: currently we prefer A100s in our core regions, but for some edge regions we need lower profile cards.
[05:30] Diego: runtime supports a range of instance types; kernel selection differs by card. we can recommend quantized variants for cost. for high concurrency we'd pick multi-GPU pools with batching and KV cache tuned.

[07:00] Samir: what's the typical pilot timeline? we want a 6-week pilot with a simple success criteria: throughput >= 500 rps sustained for 15 minutes with 99th latency under X and no quality regressions.
[07:12] Nora: that aligns with our usual pilot cadence: week 0-1 planning and infra setup, week 2-3 perf runs and tuning, week 4-5 integration with your routing, week 6 validation and handoff.
[07:25] Samir: great. what do you need from us to start?
[07:30] Nora: network diagram, list of regions, expected token budget, SSO contact, and initial list of models you intend to serve. we'll produce a SOW and pilot plan.

[09:00] Lena: curious about billing granularity — can we get partner-level reports per-tenant, per-model?
[09:10] Diego: yes — token-level breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards, and partner facing usage exports. you can also configure cost attribution keys.

[10:40] Mark: what about data residency? some customers demand EU-only processing and logs.
[10:48] Nora: you can pin processing to regions and enable Private deployment in EU regions. logs can be configured to stay in-region for Private. hosted has region options but less control than Private.

[12:00] Samir: any reseller revenue share or margins we should expect?
[12:08] Nora: we typically discuss partner economics during commercial review — common patterns are resale margin on usage or a wholesale price + cut. we'll introduce GTM folks if this moves to commercial.

[13:20] Priya: technical deep-dive — Diego will walk through the proposed network flow and pilot topology. (screen share referenced: https://redwood.example.com/decks/vb-integration.pdf)
[13:35] Diego: i'll sketch a baseline: VB will create a VPC peering connection to a Redwood ingress endpoint or use private link. traffic can be NATed through your egress so IP allowlists remain under your control. inside Dedicated, we allocate GPU worker pools with autoscale policies. request routing goes through the control plane where policy eval happens.
[14:00] Mark: do you require the TLS termination on your side or ours?
[14:05] Diego: we support both. for Private/VPC mode customers often terminate TLS on their side and use mTLS to the control plane. for hosted we manage TLS and provide certs.

[17:30] Samir: a couple of micro-questions i heard in the doc: how does KV cache persist across restarts? and is it per-tenant?
[17:40] Diego: KV cache is shardable and can be persisted to local SSD or to a backing store depending on the deployment. in Dedicated/Private it's per-customer by default. in hosted it's logically partitioned. persistence options affect recovery time after node restarts.

[20:00] Lena: about model onboarding — can we bring custom models or only from your catalog?
[20:07] Nora: both. Redwood has a curated model catalog, but partners/customers can bring their own models. for Private you can bring models and we support pinned versions, rollout policies, and evals to monitor quality regressions.

[23:15] Mark: network egress cost — if we route via you, who bears egress?
[23:22] Nora: in reseller/onramp models we usually reconcile egress by contract—if you proxy through your network, you incur egress; if traffic exits through Redwood public endpoints, Redwood's egress policy applies. we'll detail options in the SOW.

[25:00] Samir: any red flags about our proposed hybrid regions? we listed eu-west1, us-west2, ap-southeast1.
[25:10] Diego: that's fine. note some hardware types may not be available in all regions; we can provide a region-hardware matrix. expect different latency/cost profiles per region.

[28:30] Priya: for the pilot we'll recommend test prompts and evaluation harnesses — we want to avoid quality regressions while quantizing.
[28:40] Lena: yes quality matters more than small cost savings for now.

[30:00] Mark: SSOT for model configs — do you have an API for model versioning and rollouts?
[30:08] Diego: yes, model lifecycle APIs for version pinning, canary rollouts, A/B and automatic fallback policies. the console shows history and traces for inference traces.

[33:45] Samir: ok last bit — compliance paperwork. we need SOC2, ISO27001, and a PTA for shared responsiblities.
[33:55] Nora: we'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO documents in the security pack. PTA we'll iterate; expect the Private deployment to have a bit more to sign due to network access.

[36:00] Ivy: do you capture raw request/response payloads in logs? some customers require no PII retention.
[36:08] Diego: logs can be configured — we have token-level telemetry and you can disable raw payload capture, mask PII, and set retention windows. for Private you can route logs to your own syslog/ELK.

[39:20] Nora: wrap-up — quick recap and next steps?
[39:25] Samir: recap: VB to share network diagram and region list; Redwood to share security pack and pilot SOW; Redwood to provide perf harness and bench scripts; schedule kickoff.
[39:40] Nora: correct — action items captured. rough timeline we discussed — hope to start infra week of March 8th.

[40:10] Mark: one small follow-up — can you share an example of a per-tenant billing CSV?
[40:18] Nora: yes, we'll attach an example usage export (CSV) in the follow-up email.

[42:00] Priya: note: for the pilot we'll likely use a small LLM variant for initial smoke then scale to the target models. we'll share recommended quantization profiles.

[45:10] Samir: perfect. thanks everyone. look forward to the pack.
[45:15] Nora: thanks all — we'll send the deck and SOW, and propose March 8th for the pilot kickoff.
[45:25] Lena: thanks. bye.
